industry: Electrical Equipment & Parts / Data Center Infrastructure
thesis: Vertiv Holdings is a high-conviction BUY as the closest pure-play on the physical layer of the AI data center buildout — power management, thermal/liquid cooling, and integrated modular infrastructure. FY2025 revenue grew ~28% to $10.23B with net income up ~169% to $1.33B, and organic orders and backlog continue to accelerate as hyperscalers and neoclouds race to deploy high-density GPU racks that require Vertiv's liquid-cooling and power distribution. The stock is richly valued (~68x trailing, ~40x forward P/E) and highly volatile (beta ~2.0), but the multi-year secular demand for AI-ready power and cooling supports continued outperformance. Analyst consensus is Strong Buy with a ~$376 average target; our base case is $340–380 with a bull case of $400–440.

drivers: AI data center capex sustains 25%+ order growth through 2027 as hyperscalers and neoclouds deploy dense GPU clusters requiring liquid cooling
Liquid-cooling attach rate accelerates and Vertiv captures majority share of the thermal management transition from air to liquid
Operating margins expand toward 20%+ as scale, pricing, and mix improve
Backlog and book-to-bill remain above 1.0x, extending multi-year revenue visibility
Bolt-on M&A (ThermoKey, Strategic Thermal Labs, Great Lakes) deepens the thermal and rack portfolio and expands EMEA/APAC capacity

base_case.assumptions: AI infrastructure demand stays robust but order growth moderates to 15–25% YoY; Vertiv holds its leadership in power and cooling; operating margins expand modestly to the high-teens; the stock trades at ~30–38x forward EPS as the market pays a premium for the pure-play data center infrastructure exposure but not an unlimited multiple. Aligns with the ~$376 analyst consensus target.

risks: AI capex cycle peaks or pauses as hyperscalers digest prior spend, cutting order growth sharply
Competition from Schneider Electric, Eaton, and nVent compresses pricing and share in power and cooling
Hyperscaler customer concentration means a single deferral materially dents bookings
Multiple compression from ~40x forward to ~20–25x on any growth deceleration given beta ~2.0
Tariffs, component costs, and supply-chain disruptions pressure margins

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings (before market open) — organic orders, book-to-bill, backlog, and updated full-year guidance
Q3 2026 earnings — liquid-cooling ramp and margin trajectory
NVIDIA next-gen GPU (Rubin) deployments driving demand for higher-density liquid cooling and power
New manufacturing capacity (Italy, Malaysia) ramps and bolt-on acquisitions integrate
Full-year 2026 orders and backlog update; 2027 guidance framework

key_risks: AI capex cyclicality — Vertiv's growth is tightly coupled to hyperscaler and neocloud data center spending, which could pause or peak
Valuation risk — ~68x trailing and ~40x forward P/E leave little margin for error; a growth miss could trigger sharp multiple compression
High volatility — beta of ~2.0 means the stock amplifies market and sector swings
Competition from Schneider Electric, Eaton, and nVent in power and thermal management
Customer concentration — a limited number of large hyperscaler customers drive a significant share of orders
Margin pressure from tariffs, component inflation, and rapid capacity expansion
Execution risk integrating multiple bolt-on acquisitions
